name: Lechweg Wanderweg
kurzbeschreibung: The Lechweg in the Tyrolean Außerfern: long-distance hiking through the Naturpark Tiroler Lech with the 200 m Holzgau suspension bridge and wild river landscape.
beschreibung:
Overview

The Lechweg section in the Tyrolean Außerfern forms the glorious core of the 125-kilometre European long-distance trail. Stretching from Steeg at the provincial border with Vorarlberg across Holzgau, Elbigenalp, Weißenbach, and Lechaschau/Reutte, this certified Leading Quality Trail guides hikers through one of Central Europe's last remaining untamed wild river landscapes. Designed as a moderate long-distance path, the route follows the steadily widening Lech downstream, delighting nature lovers with dramatic suspension footbridges, biodiverse alluvial forests, and the incomparable rush of emerald-green mountain waters.

Naturpark Tiroler Lech & Suspension Bridge Spectacle

For miles on end, the trail winds directly through the Naturpark Tiroler Lech: here, the wild river still enjoys the freedom to naturally shift its gravel bed after every high-water surge. The expansive gravel banks and dynamically shifting gravel islands provide a sanctuary for critically endangered alpine flora and fauna, including the little ringed plover, the common sandpiper, and the rare Deutsche Tamariske (German tamarisk). Unrivaled highlights of the journey are the spectacular gorge crossings: near Holzgau, hikers cross the deep Höhenbachtalschlucht canyon on the Hängebrücke Holzgau at a dizzying height of 110 metres—measuring 200.5 metres in length, it ranks among Austria's longest pedestrian suspension bridges. Further downstream near Forchach, a 75-metre-long suspension bridge sways above the roaring currents of the Lech. Near Weißenbach and Lechaschau/Reutte, the valley basin expands into expansive natural floodplains, before the trail continues past the Pflach birdwatching tower and the mystical Alpsee to its grand finale at Lechfall near Füssen.

Visit & Getting There

The prime hiking season in the Außerfern spans from mid-May to late October. The entire Lechweg is open and freely accessible free of charge (crossing the suspension bridges is likewise free of admission). The total distance of 125 km is typically divided into six to eight daily stages of 12 to 18 kilometres each. A decisive advantage: the regional Lechbus (VVT route 110) runs throughout the entire valley, transporting hikers flexibly between lodgings and stage trailheads (free of charge with the Lechtal Guest Card). By car: via the B198 (Lechtalstraße) from Reutte or over the Fernpass (B179). By public transport: by train to Bahnhof Reutte in Tirol, where you seamlessly board the regional Lechtalbus.

Tips

The Lechweg runs predominantly along moderate mid-mountain paths and flat riverside trails without exposed climbing passages, making it exceptionally well-suited for long-distance hiking beginners and active families. Those who prefer to bypass the Holzgau suspension bridge can comfortably navigate the ravine via a gentle hiking trail through the Höhenbachtal. Take advantage of the convenient luggage transfer services provided by regional operators to hike with just a daypack.
